create.name: Findhorn Foundation
create.bio:
The Findhorn Foundation is a Scottish spiritual charity rooted in the community that grew up beside Findhorn Bay, on the Moray coast, from 1962. Its founders, Peter and Eileen Caddy and their friend Dorothy Maclean, arrived at a caravan park there with little money and began a vegetable garden guided by Eileen's meditations and Dorothy's sense of communion with the intelligence of plants. The garden's unlikely harvests drew visitors, a community formed around daily meditation and service, and in 1972 it became a registered charity with a teaching programme shaped in part by David Spangler. Over the decades The Park grew into a well-known ecovillage, and the Foundation gained a retreat house on the Isle of Iona.

Today the Foundation teaches three core principles: inner listening, working together with nature, and love in action. Its signature offering is Experience Week, a few days of shared meals, quiet reflection, group sessions and walks among the dunes and woods of the bay, alongside weeks on purpose and inner guidance, seasonal gatherings and programmes run with partner facilitators at The Park and online. Free online meditations are held every weekday morning, and a global network called Seeds of Light meets by video twice a month. The Foundation now runs as a smaller charitable organisation alongside the independent ecovillage community.

courses.title: When We're 64: A Living Story
courses.description: A residential week at The Park during the community's birthday celebrations, working with its archive of photographs, writings and recordings and talking with long-standing members who remember the early years. Participants reflect on what the story means for their own path and help add to the living record.

courses.title: Experience Week: From I to We (December 2026)
courses.description: Findhorn's introductory residential week of shared community life, with reflective practice, group sessions, silence and time in nature. This December run, focalised by Christine Lines and Bridget O'Donnell, gives extra attention to listening and honest, compassionate communication drawn from Nonviolent Communication.

courses.title: Crossing the Threshold: A New Year's Celebration in Community
courses.description: A partner programme over New Year with musicians Barbara Swetina and Jilani Cordelia, mixing the Dances of Universal Peace, devotional singing, story, ritual and quiet reflection on the year ending and the one beginning, rooted in the Findhorn and Sufi traditions.

courses.title: Experience Week: From I to We (February 2027)
courses.description: Five days living alongside the Findhorn community in shared rooms, with communal vegetarian meals, reflective practice, group sessions, silence and walks by the dunes and bay, exploring inner listening and what changes when attention moves from 'I' to 'We'. No previous spiritual practice is needed.

courses.title: Experience Week: From I to We (March 2027)
courses.description: The spring run of Findhorn's foundation programme: a residential week of community living at The Park, with shared meals, quiet practice, group sharing and time outdoors, offered as a gentle first taste of the Findhorn way of inner listening.

courses.title: Following your Calling: Discovering purpose through Inner Listening
courses.description: A week at The Park with long-time members Mary Inglis and Christine Lines for anyone sensing a new direction in life. Shared practice, gentle questions, time in nature and the Transformation Game are used to listen for a personal sense of purpose and how present circumstances might serve it.

courses.title: Seeds of Light
courses.description: An online circle for people around the world who feel a link with Findhorn. Members meet live on Zoom twice a month for meditation, sharing in small groups and a talk from a guest in the community, and the calls are not recorded.
courses.price: Monthly or annual contribution (amount chosen at sign-up)

free_resources.title: Meditate with us
free_resources.description: A free half-hour group meditation on Zoom every weekday at 9am UK time, with replays on YouTube for those in other time zones. Sign up to receive the link.

free_resources.title: Weekday meditation replays
free_resources.description: The recorded weekday group meditations on the Findhorn Foundation's YouTube channel, to sit with at any time.

free_resources.title: Guidance from Eileen Caddy
free_resources.description: Short passages of the inner guidance co-founder Eileen Caddy received in meditation, taken from her book Opening Doors Within, to read online.

free_resources.title: Daily Inspiration Cards
free_resources.description: An online deck of 78 cards, each with a line from Eileen Caddy's guidance; draw one as a theme to reflect on for the day.

free_resources.title: Findhorn Foundation on YouTube
free_resources.description: More than 600 free videos from the Foundation, including its recorded weekday meditations, talks and films about the community.

Regional: Moray, north-east Scotland: outside London and the big cities; one Spiritpedia teacher already gives Findhorn as their base (John Philip Newell).

Founded year 1962: the community's founding year (findhorn.org/history: 'unintentionally founded the Findhorn community in 1962'). The Findhorn Foundation charitable trust was registered in 1972, and the current Findhorn Foundation SCIO (charity SC051938) is newer. Owner may prefer 1972.

Organisation change: findhorn.org's FAQ says the Foundation is moving from the old charitable trust to a SCIO, sold Cluny Hill in March 2025, and is passing Park properties to community bodies; the site's programmes are branded 'FF3' in places. The bio says it now runs as a smaller organisation beside the independent ecovillage community.
